title.zh: 卷三百十九 列傳第二百〇七 廣西土司三
title.raw: 卷三百十九 列傳第二百〇七 廣西土司三 Volume 319 Biographies 207: Guangxi Tribal Headmen 3

sentences.zh: 泗城利州龍州歸順向武奉議江州思陵

translations.literal: Sicheng, Lizhou, Longzhou, Guishun, Xiangwu, Fengyi, Jiangzhou, Siling
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng, Lizhou, Longzhou, Guishun, Xiangwu, Fengyi, Jiangzhou, and Siling

sentences.zh: （廣東瓊州府附）〉

translations.literal: (Attached under Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Attached under Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong)〉

sentences.zh: 泗城州，宋置，隸橫山寨。

translations.literal: Sicheng Prefecture was established in the Song and was subordinate to Hengshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng Prefecture was founded in the Song dynasty and placed under Hengshan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元屬田州路。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it belonged to Tianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan it fell under Tianzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其界東抵東蘭，西抵上林長官司，南抵田州，北抵永寧州。

translations.literal: Its borders: east abutting Donglan, west abutting the Shanglin Native Official Office, south abutting Tianzhou, north abutting Yongning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Donglan to the east, the Shanglin Native Official Office to the west, Tianzhou to the south, and Yongning Prefecture to the north.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年，征南副將軍周德興克泗城州，土官岑善忠歸附，授世襲知州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu, Vice General for the Southern Campaign Zhou Dexing captured Sicheng Prefecture; the native official Cen Shanzhong submitted, and was appointed hereditary prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongwu, Zhou Dexing, vice general of the southern campaign, took Sicheng Prefecture. The native official Cen Shanzhong submitted and was granted the hereditary post of prefect.

sentences.zh: 十三年，善忠子振作亂，寇利州，廣西都司討平之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Shanzhong's son Zhen raised a rebellion, raided Lizhou, and the Guangxi Regional Military Commission suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Shanzhong's son Zhen rebelled and attacked Lizhou. The Guangxi Regional Military Commission marched out and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 十四年，善忠來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Shanzhong came bearing tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Shanzhong presented tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，振遣人貢馬及方物，詔賜以鈔錠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Zhen sent men to present horses and tribute goods; an edict bestowed paper currency upon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, Zhen sent envoys with horses and local products; the throne responded with an edict awarding him paper currency.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，女土官盧氏遣族人岑臺貢馬及銀器等物，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, the female native official Lu sent her clansman Cen Tai to present horses, silver vessels, and other goods; rewards were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande, the female native official Lady Lu dispatched her kinsman Cen Tai with horses, silverware, and other gifts. The court returned gifts scaled to his station.

sentences.zh: 八年，致仕女土官盧氏奏，襲職土官岑豹率土兵千五百余人謀害己，又棄毀故土官岑瑄塑像，所為不孝，難俾襲職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the retired female native official Lu memorialized that the succession native official Cen Bao had led more than fifteen hundred native troops in plotting to kill her, and had also discarded and destroyed the image of the former native official Cen Xuan—conduct that was unfilial and made him unfit to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the retired Lady Lu submitted a memorial accusing Cen Bao, the man slated to succeed her, of leading more than fifteen hundred native soldiers in a plot against her life and of casting aside and smashing the portrait of the late native official Cen Xuan—acts so lacking in filial duty, she argued, that he ought not inherit the office at all.

sentences.zh: 豹叔利州知州顏亦奏豹興兵謀殺盧氏，州民被害。

translations.literal: Bao's uncle, Lizhou Prefect Yan, also memorialized that Bao had raised troops intending to kill Lu, and that the people of the prefecture had suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's uncle Yan, prefect of Lizhou, also reported that Bao had mobilized troops to murder Lady Lu and that the people of the prefecture had paid the price.

sentences.zh: 都督山雲奏：「豹實故土官瑄侄，人所信服，應襲職。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Shan Yun memorialized: "Bao is in fact the nephew of the former native official Xuan, whom people trust; he should inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Shan Yun wrote: "Bao is truly the nephew of the late native official Cen Xuan, a man the people respect. He should be allowed to succeed.

sentences.zh: 盧氏，瑄妻，豹伯母，初借襲，今致仕，宜量撥田土以贍終身。

translations.literal: Lu is Xuan's wife and Bao's aunt-by-marriage; she initially held the post in his stead and has now retired; she should be allotted land in appropriate measure to support her for life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu is Xuan's widow and Bao's aunt. She first held the office on his behalf and has since retired. She should receive a measured grant of fields and lands sufficient to sustain her for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 仍請敕豹無肆侵擾。

translations.literal: It is further requested that Bao be ordered by imperial edict not to encroach upon or harass her at will."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order should also forbid Bao from harassing or encroaching upon her at will."

sentences.zh: 」兵部請從雲奏。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War requested that Yun's memorial be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War recommended adopting Shan Yun's proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝命行人章聰、侯琎賫敕，諭雲會三司巡按究豹與盧氏是非，從公判決。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the envoys Zhang Cong and Hou Jin to bear an edict instructing Yun to convene the three provincial offices and the touring censor to investigate right and wrong between Bao and Lu, and render judgment impartially.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dispatched the envoys Zhang Cong and Hou Jin with an edict directing Shan Yun to assemble the three provincial offices and the touring censor, hear both sides in the dispute between Bao and Lady Lu, and decide the matter fairly.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，豹遣人入貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, Bao sent men to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong, Bao sent tribute to court.

sentences.zh: 二年，豹攻利州，掠其叔顏妻子財物。

translations.literal: In the second year, Bao attacked Lizhou and seized his uncle Yan's wife, children, and property.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Bao struck Lizhou, carrying off his uncle Yan's wife, children, and possessions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷官至撫諭，負固不服，增兵拒守。

translations.literal: Officials of the court arrived to pacify and instruct him, but he stubbornly refused to submit and added troops to resist and hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Court emissaries came to reason with him, yet he dug in and refused obedience, reinforcing his garrisons to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 雲以聞，乞發兵剿之。

translations.literal: Yun reported this and requested that troops be dispatched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Yun reported the affair and asked permission to send troops against him.

sentences.zh: 帝敕雲曰：「蠻夷梗化，罪固難容，然興師動眾，事亦不易，其更遣人諭之。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued instructions to Yun: "The barbarians' obstruction of civilization is a crime that can hardly be tolerated, yet raising armies and mobilizing masses is not easy either; send envoys again to instruct him."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied to Shan Yun: "These frontier people resist assimilation, and their offense is scarcely to be borne. Yet to raise an army is no small matter. Send envoys once more and try persuasion first."

sentences.zh: 」五年，顏奏豹侵占及掠擄罪。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yan memorialized concerning Bao's crimes of encroachment and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Yan submitted charges of seizure and looting against Bao.

sentences.zh: 頭目黃祖亦奏豹殺其弟，籍其家。

translations.literal: The chieftain Huang Zu also memorialized that Bao had killed his younger brother and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Huang Zu likewise accused Bao of murdering his younger brother and seizing his family's property.

sentences.zh: 瑄女亦奏豹占奪田地人民，囚其母盧氏。

translations.literal: Xuan's daughter also memorialized that Bao had seized lands and people, and imprisoned her mother Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Xuan's daughter also charged that Bao had taken fields and subjects by force and imprisoned her mother, Lady Lu.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣行人朱升、黃恕齋敕諭之，並敕廣西、貴州總兵官親詣其地，令速還所侵掠，如不服，相機擒捕。

translations.literal: The Emperor again dispatched the envoys Zhu Sheng and Huang Shu bearing an edict to instruct him, and also ordered the regional commanders of Guangxi and Guizhou to go in person to the place, commanding the swift return of what had been seized; if he would not submit, they were to seize him as opportunity allowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent Zhu Sheng and Huang Shu with an edict of admonition, and ordered the regional commanders of Guangxi and Guizhou to go in person, demand the immediate return of everything taken, and, should he still refuse, capture him when the moment served.

sentences.zh: 六年，總兵官柳溥奏：「行人恕、升同廣西三司委官諭豹退還原占利州地，豹時面從，及回，占如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Regional Commander Liu Pu memorialized: "The envoys Shu and Sheng, together with officials delegated by the three Guangxi offices, instructed Bao to withdraw and return the Lizhou lands he had originally occupied; Bao outwardly agreed at the time, but after they left, the occupation remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Regional Commander Liu Pu reported: "The envoys Huang Shu and Zhu Sheng, acting with delegates from the three Guangxi provincial offices, ordered Bao to restore the Lizhou lands he had seized. He agreed to their faces, but once they were gone his occupation continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 今顏欲以利州、利甲等莊易泗城、古那等甲，開設利州衙門，宜從其請，發附近官軍送顏赴彼撫治蠻民。

translations.literal: Now Yan wishes to exchange the Lizhou and Lijia and other estates for the Sicheng, Guna, and other estates, and establish a Lizhou yamen—it is appropriate to grant his request, dispatch nearby regular troops to escort Yan there to pacify and govern the barbarian people.
translations.idiomatic: Yan now proposes to swap the Lizhou and Lijia estates for Sicheng, Guna, and the other holdings, and to set up a Lizhou yamen there. His request should be granted, and nearby regular troops should escort him to the site to govern the native population.

sentences.zh: 倘豹仍拒逆，則率兵剿捕。

translations.literal: If Bao still resists, then lead troops to suppress and capture him."
translations.idiomatic: If Bao continues to defy the court, troops should be sent to suppress him and take him captive."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 八年，豹遣人奉貢，賜彩幣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Bao sent men bearing tribute; colored silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Bao sent tribute envoys and received colored silks in return.

sentences.zh: 十年，豹復奏顏占據其地，帝令速予議處，不可因循，貽邊方害。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Bao again memorialized that Yan was occupying his lands; the Emperor ordered that the matter be settled quickly by deliberation—it must not be allowed to drag on and bring harm to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Bao again complained that Yan was holding his territory. The Emperor commanded a swift settlement and warned that delay would only endanger the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，豹聚眾四萬，攻劫上林長官司，殺土官岑誌威，據其境土。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Bao gathered forty thousand men, attacked and looted the Shanglin Native Official Office, killed the native official Cen Zhiwei, and seized its territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua, Bao mustered forty thousand followers, stormed the Shanglin Native Official Office, killed its native official Cen Zhiwei, and annexed the district.

sentences.zh: 兵部言：「豹強獷如此，宜調兵擒捕，明正典刑。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War stated: "Bao is so violent and fierce; troops should be mobilized to capture him and apply the law clearly."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War argued: "Bao's brutality has gone this far. Troops should be called up to seize him and punish him according to law."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation was accepted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，豹死。

translations.literal: Before long, Bao died.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, Bao died.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，土官知州岑應復據上林長官司及貴州鎮寧等處一十八城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi, the native prefect Cen Ying again occupied the Shanglin Native Official Office and eighteen walled settlements including Zhenning in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi, the native prefect Cen Ying once more seized the Shanglin Native Official Office and eighteen walled settlements in Guizhou, among them Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 時恩城土官岑欽攻奪田州府，逐知府岑溥。

translations.literal: At the time the Encheng native official Cen Qin attacked and seized Tianzhou Prefecture, driving out Prefect Cen Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Encheng native official Cen Qin attacked Tianzhou Prefecture, took it by force, and expelled its prefect, Cen Pu.

sentences.zh: 應與欽黨，既復相仇，兩家父子交相仇殺。

translations.literal: Ying and Qin were allies, then became enemies again; the two families' fathers and sons killed one another in mutual vendetta.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Qin had been allies, then turned on each other; fathers and sons in both houses slaughtered one another in an escalating feud.

sentences.zh: 事聞，兵部奏：「欽連年構禍，而應黨之，復據上林長官司，流毒不少，今天厭禍，假手相殘，實地方之幸。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, the Ministry of War memorialized: "Qin has stirred up calamity year after year, and Ying allied with him; he has again occupied the Shanglin Native Official Office, spreading poison far and wide. Now Heaven loathes such calamity and has used their hands to destroy one another—this is truly fortune for the region.
translations.idiomatic: When reports reached the capital, the Ministry of War wrote: "Qin has brought trouble year after year, and Ying stood with him. Ying has again taken the Shanglin Native Official Office and spread ruin across the countryside. Heaven now seems to abhor the disorder and has set them to destroying one another—a piece of good fortune for the region.

sentences.zh: 應所占鄰壤及土官印信數多，亦宜勘斷，以除禍本，並令應弟接退還侵地及印信，乃許承襲。

translations.literal: The neighboring lands Ying has occupied and the numerous native official seals also ought to be surveyed and adjudicated to remove the root of calamity; his younger brother Jie should be ordered to return seized lands and seals before succession may be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring territories Ying holds and the many native seals he has taken should also be surveyed and settled, uprooting the source of the trouble. Only after Ying's younger brother Jie returns the seized lands and seals should succession even be considered.

sentences.zh: 泗城地廣兵多，宜選頭目，量授職銜，分轄以殺其勢。

translations.literal: Sicheng's territory is broad and its troops numerous; chieftains should be selected and titles granted in measured degrees, with divided jurisdiction to reduce its power.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng sprawls across a wide domain and fields a strong force. Headmen should be chosen, titles meted out in proportion, and authority divided among them to break its power.

sentences.zh: 」詔下總鎮官區處。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for the supreme regional commander to arrange matters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out directing the supreme regional commander to handle the matter.

sentences.zh: 接遣人朝正，賜彩緞鈔錠。

translations.literal: Jie sent men to attend the New Year's audience; colored silk and paper currency were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sent representatives to the New Year's audience at court and received colored silk and paper currency in return.

sentences.zh: 十年，總督鄧廷瓚奏：「接往年隨征都勻、府江等處有功，乞略其祖父罪，令承襲世職，以圖報效。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Governor Deng Tingzan memorialized: "Jie in past years followed campaigns at Duyun, Fujiang, and other places with merit; it is requested that his grandfather's crimes be overlooked and he be allowed to inherit the hereditary post, that he may repay service."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Governor Deng Tingzan petitioned: "Jie served with distinction in earlier campaigns at Duyun, Fujiang, and elsewhere. I ask that his grandfather's offenses be set aside and that he be permitted to inherit the hereditary office, so that he may prove his loyalty in service."

sentences.zh: 」廷臣議：「劫印侵地，雖系接祖父罪，然再四撫諭，接不肯歸之於官，遽使襲職，則誌益驕，非馭土官法。」

translations.literal: Court officials deliberated: "Seizing seals and encroaching on lands, though crimes of Jie's grandfather, yet after repeated pacification and instruction Jie still refuses to return them to the government; to hastily grant him succession would only make his ambition more arrogant—it is not the method for governing native officials."
translations.idiomatic: The court deliberated and replied: "The theft of seals and seizure of territory belong to the crimes of Jie's grandfather, yet even after repeated persuasion Jie will not restore them to the government. To grant him succession now would only swell his pride. That is no way to govern native officials."

sentences.zh: 十二年，田州土目黃驥作亂，要接為聲援，殺掠男婦，劫燒倉庫民廬，又劫府學及橫山驛印記，遂據興仁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Tianzhou native chieftain Huang Ji rebelled, demanding Jie as his support; he killed and plundered men and women, looted and burned storehouses and civilian dwellings, also seized the seals of the prefectural school and Hengshan Post Station, and then occupied Xingren.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Tianzhou chieftain Huang Ji rose in rebellion and called on Jie for support. He killed and plundered, burned storehouses and homes, seized the seals of the prefectural school and Hengshan Post Station, and finally took Xingren.

sentences.zh: 十四年，貴州賊婦米魯作亂，提督王軾請調接領土兵二萬營於砦布河，因敕接自備兩月餉，克期赴調。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Guizhou bandit woman Mi Lu rebelled; Grand Coordinator Wang Zhi requested that Jie be mobilized to lead twenty thousand native troops and encamp at Zhaibu River; accordingly Jie was ordered to supply two months' rations himself and meet the mobilization deadline.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the Guizhou rebel Mi Lu took up arms. Grand Coordinator Wang Zhi asked that Jie be called up to lead twenty thousand native soldiers to camp at Zhaibu River. Jie was ordered to provision his men for two months out of his own stores and report on schedule.

sentences.zh: 十八年，泗城土官族人岑九仙奏：「自始祖岑彭以來，世襲土官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Sicheng native official clansman Cen Jiuxian memorialized: "Since the founding ancestor Cen Peng, native officials have been hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, a Sicheng clansman named Cen Jiuxian submitted a memorial: "From our founding ancestor Cen Peng down, the native office has passed from father to son.

sentences.zh: 至豹子應罹欽之禍，子孫滅亡殆盡，其弟接，眾推護印，累著勞勚，乞令襲職，俾掌轄蠻眾。

translations.literal: When Bao's son Ying suffered calamity from Qin, descendants were nearly all destroyed; his younger brother Jie, whom the multitude urged to guard the seal, has repeatedly shown merit; it is requested that he be allowed to inherit the post and govern the barbarian masses."
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Ying met disaster through Qin, and the line was all but wiped out. His younger brother Jie, whom the people pressed to safeguard the seal, has since rendered repeated service. I beg that he be confirmed in office and entrusted with rule over the native clans."

sentences.zh: 」兵部尚書劉大夏等議：「豹乃叛臣余孽，子應復自取滅亡。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Daxia and others deliberated: "Bao was the remnant offspring of a rebellious minister; his son Ying again brought destruction upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liu Daxia and his colleagues replied: "Bao was the scion of a traitor, and his son Ying courted ruin of his own making.

sentences.zh: 今接者，人皆傳稱為梁接，非應親枝，又不知岑九仙是何逋逃，冒為奏擾。

translations.literal: As for the present Jie, everyone says he is called Liang Jie—not a direct branch of Ying; and who knows what fugitive Cen Jiuxian is, falsely memorializing to stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: This man now called Jie is widely said to be Liang Jie, not a direct descendant of Ying at all. As for Cen Jiuxian, who can say what runaway he is, filing false petitions to stir up trouble?

sentences.zh: 臣大夏先在兩廣，見岑氏譜。

translations.literal: Minister Daxia was formerly in the Two Guangs and saw the Cen clan genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: I, Daxia, served earlier in the Two Guangs and examined the Cen clan genealogy myself.

sentences.zh: 岑之始祖木納罕於元至正年間，與田州知府之祖伯顏，一時受官。

translations.literal: The Cen founding ancestor Munahan, in the Zhizheng period of the Yuan, received office at the same time as the ancestor of the Tianzhou prefect, Boliyan.
translations.idiomatic: The Cens trace their origin to Munahan, who received office in the Zhizheng era of the Yuan at the same time as Boliyan, ancestor of the Tianzhou prefectural line.

sentences.zh: 今九仙妄援漢岑彭世次，塵瀆聖聽，請治其罪。

translations.literal: Now Jiuxian falsely cites the Han Dynasty Cen Peng's lineal descent, sullying the Emperor's ears; his crime should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxian now falsely claims descent from the Han general Cen Peng, polluting what reaches the throne. He should be punished for it.

sentences.zh: 其岑接應襲與否，前已令鎮巡官勘奏，岑九仙雖蠻人難以深究，亦當摘發以破其奸。

translations.literal: As for whether Cen Jie should inherit, this was already ordered investigated and memorialized by the regional pacification officials; though Jiuxian is a barbarian and hard to examine thoroughly, his fraud should still be exposed to break his deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Cen Jie ought to succeed has already been referred to the frontier pacification officials for investigation. Jiuxian may be a barbarian and difficult to examine closely, but his imposture should still be exposed and his scheme broken.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年，泗城及程縣各遣官族來貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde, Sicheng and Cheng County each sent official clansmen to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengde, Sicheng and Cheng County each dispatched clansmen bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 後期，賞減半。

translations.literal: They were late; rewards were halved.
translations.idiomatic: They arrived late, and their rewards were cut in half.

sentences.zh: 泗城貢厚，仍全給之。

translations.literal: Sicheng's tribute was substantial, so the full reward was still given.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sicheng's tribute was unusually generous, the court paid the full reward all the same.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，田州岑猛率兵攻泗城，拔六寨，進薄州城，克之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Tianzhou's Cen Meng led troops to attack Sicheng, captured six stockades, advanced close to the prefectural seat, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, Cen Meng of Tianzhou marched on Sicheng, took six stockades, pressed up to the prefectural city, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 接告急軍門，言猛無故攻寨。

translations.literal: Jie reported in emergency to the military headquarters, saying Meng had attacked the stockades without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Jie sent an urgent appeal to the military headquarters, protesting that Meng had attacked his stockades without provocation.

sentences.zh: 猛言接非岑氏後，據其祖業，欲得所侵地。

translations.literal: Meng stated that Jie was not of the Cen line, was holding their ancestral domain, and wanted to recover the lands that had been seized.
translations.idiomatic: Meng countered that Jie was no true Cen, that he occupied their ancestral domain, and that he sought to recover lands wrongly taken from them.

sentences.zh: 詔下勘處。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for investigation and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered an inquiry and settlement.

sentences.zh: 十六年，田州盧蘇作亂。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Tianzhou's Lu Su rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Lu Su of Tianzhou rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 泗城土舍岑施以兵納岑邦佐。

translations.literal: The Sicheng tusi assistant Cen Shi led troops to install Cen Bangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Sicheng native assistant Cen Shi marched with troops to install Cen Bangzuo in office.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，弗克納。

translations.literal: The troops were defeated and could not install him.
translations.idiomatic: His force was beaten and failed to place Bangzuo on the seat.

sentences.zh: 二十七年詔土舍施襲替，免赴京，以嘗聽調有勞也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year an edict granted the tusi assistant Shi succession to the post, exempting him from journeying to the capital, because he had once heeded mobilization with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year an edict confirmed Shi's succession, excusing him from traveling to the capital because he had answered a prior call to arms with creditable service.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，泗城蠻黃豹、黃豸等據貴州程番府麻向、大華等司，時出擄掠，官軍剿之，豹等遁去。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing, the Sicheng barbarians Huang Bao, Huang Zhi, and others occupied Mahxiang, Dahua, and other offices of Guizhou's Chenfan Prefecture, raiding from time to time; regular troops suppressed them and Bao and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing, the Sicheng bandits Huang Bao, Huang Zhi, and their followers seized Mahxiang, Dahua, and other districts under Guizhou's Chenfan Prefecture, raiding whenever they could. Regular troops moved against them, and Bao and his men fled.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，泗城土官岑承勛等貢馬及香爐等物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, the Sicheng native officials Cen Chengxun and others presented horses, incense burners, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli, the Sicheng native officials Cen Chengxun and others sent horses, incense burners, and other tribute.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，土官岑雲漢貢方物。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the native official Cen Yunhan presented tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year, the native official Cen Yunhan presented local products to court.

sentences.zh: 初，雲漢乃紹勛嫡嗣，紹勛寵庶孽雷漢，頭目黃瑪等從中煽禍，以至焚劫稱兵。

translations.literal: Initially, Yunhan was Chengxun's legitimate heir; Chengxun favored the bastard Lei Han, and chieftains including Huang Ma fanned trouble from within, until there was burning, looting, and raising of arms.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yunhan was Chengxun's legitimate heir, but Chengxun doted on his bastard son Lei Han. Headmen such as Huang Ma stoked the quarrel from within until the affair erupted into arson, plunder, and open war.

sentences.zh: 雲漢紿母出印，扶弟以奔，撫按以聞。

translations.literal: Yunhan deceived his mother into producing the seal, supported his younger brother and fled; the grand coordinator and provincial inspector reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Yunhan tricked his mother into yielding the seal, then fled with his younger brother in tow. The grand coordinator and provincial inspector reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 廷議請釋紹勛罪以存大倫，權雷漢、黃瑪等以息囂孽，雲漢從寬削銜，戴罪管事。

translations.literal: Court deliberation requested releasing Chengxun from punishment to preserve the great ethical order, temporarily restraining Lei Han, Huang Ma, and others to quiet the unruly offspring; Yunhan, treated leniently, had his title reduced and was allowed to manage affairs while bearing his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation favored pardoning Chengxun to preserve family order, temporarily restraining Lei Han, Huang Ma, and the other troublemakers, and treating Yunhan leniently by reducing his rank while allowing him to govern under suspended punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，巡撫何士晉請復雲漢知州職，量加都司職銜，令率土兵援黔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, Grand Coordinator He Shijin requested restoring Yunhan to the post of prefect, adding a Regional Military Commission title in measured degree, and ordering him to lead native troops to aid Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi, Grand Coordinator He Shijin asked that Yunhan be restored as prefect, given an appropriate Regional Military Commission title, and ordered to lead native troops to the aid of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 泗城延袤頗廣，兵力亦勁，與慶遠諸州互相雄長。

translations.literal: Sicheng's extent is quite broad and its military strength formidable; it vies for dominance with the various prefectures of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng sprawls across a wide territory and commands a formidable force; it contends for supremacy with the prefectures of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 其流惡自豹而應而接，且三世。

translations.literal: Its reign of evil passed from Bao to Ying to Jie—three generations in all.
translations.idiomatic: Its trail of violence ran from Bao to Ying to Jie—three generations without break.

sentences.zh: 領縣一，曰程縣；

translations.literal: It administers one county, called Cheng County;
translations.idiomatic: It governed one county, Cheng County;

sentences.zh: 長官司二，曰安隆，曰上林。

translations.literal: and two native official offices: Anlong and Shanglin.
translations.idiomatic: and two native official districts, Anlong and Shanglin.

sentences.zh: 程縣在泗城州之東北，舊號程醜莊。

translations.literal: Cheng County lies northeast of Sicheng Prefecture; it was formerly called Cheng Chou Estate.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng County stood northeast of Sicheng Prefecture and was once known as Cheng Chou Estate.

sentences.zh: 明初歸附，隸泗城州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming it submitted and was subordinate to Sicheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming it submitted and was placed under Sicheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十一年改為縣，編戶一里。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Hongwu it was converted to a county, with one li of registered households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Hongwu it was made a county with one li of registered households.

sentences.zh: 後改屬慶遠府，尋復隸泗城州，設流官知縣。

translations.literal: Later it was transferred to Qingyuan Prefecture, then soon restored to Sicheng Prefecture, with a regular official prefect appointed.
translations.idiomatic: It was later transferred to Qingyuan Prefecture, then soon returned to Sicheng's jurisdiction, with a regular magistrate appointed to govern it.

sentences.zh: 正統間，為岑豹所逼，棄官遁去，典史攝印，旋亦罹害。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, pressed by Cen Bao, the magistrate abandoned his post and fled; the registrar held the seal in his stead and soon also fell victim.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, harried by Cen Bao, the magistrate fled his post. The registrar took charge of the seal and soon met the same fate.

sentences.zh: 豹遂奪其印，據縣治。

translations.literal: Bao then seized the seal and occupied the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Bao then seized the seal and took over the county seat.

sentences.zh: 事聞，屢遣官諭之，歷岑應、岑接凡七十余年不服。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, officials were repeatedly dispatched to instruct him; through Cen Ying and Cen Jie, for more than seventy years, he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the capital, the court sent envoy after envoy to reason with him, yet through the reigns of Cen Ying and Cen Jie—for more than seventy years—he never yielded.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，接為諸土官攻殺，督府遣官按問，得縣印，貯於官，後僅存荒土。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Jie was attacked and killed by various native officials; the governor-general dispatched officials to investigate, recovered the county seal, and stored it in the government office; afterward only wasteland remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, rival native officials attacked and killed Jie. The governor-general sent investigators, recovered the county seal, and placed it in government custody. Nothing remained of the county but empty land.

sentences.zh: 泗城、南丹、那地俱欲得之，時治兵相攻雲。

translations.literal: Sicheng, Nandan, and Nadi all wanted to obtain it; at times they readied troops and attacked one another without end.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng, Nandan, and Nadi all coveted the territory and repeatedly mobilized troops to fight one another over it.

sentences.zh: 安隆長官司，東抵泗城，西抵雲南，南抵上林長官司，北抵貴州宣慰司，元泗城州地也。

translations.literal: The Anlong Native Official Office: east abutting Sicheng, west abutting Yunnan, south abutting the Shanglin Native Official Office, north abutting the Guizhou Pacification Commission—territory that was Sicheng Prefecture under the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Anlong Native Official Office bordered Sicheng on the east, Yunnan on the west, the Shanglin Native Official Office on the south, and the Guizhou Pacification Commission on the north—lands that had formed part of Sicheng Prefecture under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，泗城州土官岑善忠以次子子得領安隆峒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongwu, the Sicheng native official Cen Shanzhong had his second son Zide take charge of the Anlong dong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongwu, the Sicheng native official Cen Shanzhong put his second son Zide in charge of the Anlong district.

sentences.zh: 三十年，子得來朝，貢馬。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Zide came to court and presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, Zide came to court and presented horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 設治所。

translations.literal: A governing post was established.
translations.idiomatic: A local administrative seat was established.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年設安隆長官事，以子得為長官，撫其眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Anlong native official post was established, with Zide as native official to pacify the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle the post of Anlong native official was created, with Zide appointed to govern and pacify the people.

sentences.zh: 十二年貢馬，賜鈔幣，予世襲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he presented horses; paper currency was bestowed and hereditary succession granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he sent horses as tribute; the court returned paper currency and granted hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 龍州，古百粵地。

translations.literal: Longzhou: ancient land of the Baiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhou was ancient territory of the Baiyue peoples.

sentences.zh: 漢屬交阯。

translations.literal: Under the Han it belonged to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han it formed part of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 宋置龍州，隸太平寨。

translations.literal: The Song established Longzhou, subordinate to Taiping Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Song founded Longzhou and placed it under Taiping Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元大德中，升州為萬戶府。

translations.literal: In the Dade era of the Yuan, the prefecture was promoted to a Myriad Household Command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan Dade reign, Longzhou was elevated from a prefecture to a Myriad Household Command.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年，龍州土官趙帖堅遣使奉表，貢方物。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 2, the native official of Longzhou Zhao Tie Jian sent envoys bearing a memorial and tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 2, Zhao Tie Jian, the native official of Longzhou, dispatched envoys with a formal submission and local tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔以帖堅為龍州知州，世襲。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Tie Jian prefect of Longzhou, with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Tie Jian prefect of Longzhou, with the office to pass down in his line.

sentences.zh: 八年改隸廣西布政司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was reassigned to the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Hongwu, Longzhou was placed under the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 時帖堅言：「地臨交阯，所守關隘二十七處，有警須申報太平，達總司，比報下，已涉旬月，恐誤事機，乞依奉議、泗城二州，隸廣西便。

translations.literal: At that time Tie Jian said: "The territory borders Jiaozhi, and the passes we guard number twenty-seven. When there is an alarm we must report to Taiping, reach the supreme command, and by the time the reply comes down a full ten-day month has passed, so I fear opportunities will be missed. I beg that, like Fengyi and Sicheng, it be made convenient to be subordinate to Guangxi."
translations.idiomatic: Tie Jian then explained that Longzhou lay on the Jiaozhi frontier and guarded twenty-seven passes. Any alarm had to be reported through Taiping to the supreme command, and by the time orders returned a month might have passed—too slow for military needs. He asked that Longzhou, like Fengyi and Sicheng, be placed directly under Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十六年，帖堅以孝慈皇后喪，上慰表，貢馬及方物，賜綺帛鈔錠有差。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because of the mourning for Empress Xiaoci, Tie Jian submitted a memorial of condolence, presented horses and tribute goods, and received graded gifts of silk, brocade, and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, after the death of Empress Xiaoci, Tie Jian sent a memorial of condolence together with horses and local tribute, and was rewarded with graded gifts of silk, brocade, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，帖堅病，無子，以其從子宗壽代署州事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Tie Jian fell ill. Having no son, he had his nephew Zongshou act in his stead to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Tie Jian fell ill. With no son of his own, he put his nephew Zongshou in charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 帖堅卒，宗壽襲。

translations.literal: When Tie Jian died, Zongshou succeeded to the office.
translations.idiomatic: After Tie Jian's death, Zongshou inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 鄭國公常茂以罪謫居龍州。

translations.literal: Duke of Zheng Guo Chang Mao was banished for a crime to live at Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Mao, Duke of Zheng, was punished for a crime and exiled to Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 帖堅妻黃氏有二女，一為太平州土官李圓泰妻，茂納其一為妾。

translations.literal: Tie Jian's wife, Lady Huang, had two daughters. One was the wife of Li Yuantai, native official of Taiping Prefecture, and Mao took the other as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Jian's widow, Lady Huang, had two daughters. One had married Li Yuantai, the native official of Taiping Prefecture; Chang Mao took the other as his concubine.

sentences.zh: 時宗壽雖襲職，帖堅妻猶持土官印，與茂、圓泰專擅州事，數陵逼宗壽。

translations.literal: At the time, although Zongshou had succeeded to office, Tie Jian's wife still held the native official's seal and, together with Mao and Yuantai, monopolized prefectural affairs, repeatedly bullying Zongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Although Zongshou had already taken office, Tie Jian's widow still kept the native seal. She, Chang Mao, and Yuantai together controlled the prefecture and repeatedly humiliated Zongshou.

sentences.zh: 會茂以病卒，其閽者趙觀海等亦肆侮宗壽。

translations.literal: When Mao died of illness, his gatekeeper Zhao Guanhai and others also wantonly insulted Zongshou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang Mao died of illness, even his gatekeeper Zhao Guanhai and others openly abused Zongshou.

sentences.zh: 宗壽乃與把事等以計取土官印，上奏，言茂已死，並械觀海等至京。

translations.literal: Zongshou then joined with the bashi and others in a stratagem to seize the native official's seal, memorialized the throne, reported that Mao was already dead, and sent Guanhai and the others to the capital in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshou then worked with the bashi and other local officers to seize the native seal by stratagem. He memorialized the throne that Mao was dead and had Guanhai and the others escorted to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 於是帖堅妻惶懼，使人告宗壽擄掠，又與圓泰謀劫茂妾並其奴婢往太平州，又盡掠趙氏祖父官誥諸物，又欲並取龍州之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tie Jian's wife, in alarm, sent men to accuse Zongshou of plunder, and together with Yuantai plotted to seize Mao's concubine along with her male and female servants and take them to Taiping Prefecture. They also carried off all the Zhao family's ancestral patents of office and other objects, and further sought to annex Longzhou itself.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Jian's widow, terrified, accused Zongshou of looting and conspired with Yuantai to abduct Chang Mao's concubine and her servants to Taiping Prefecture. She also stripped away the Zhao family's ancestral patents of office and other possessions, and even tried to seize Longzhou itself.

sentences.zh: 乃自至京，告宗壽實從子，不應襲，宗壽亦上章言狀。

translations.literal: She then came in person to the capital and reported that Zongshou was in fact a nephew and ought not to succeed; Zongshou also submitted a memorial stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: She went to the capital herself to claim that Zongshou, being only a nephew, had no right to inherit. Zongshou submitted his own memorial setting out the facts.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔宗壽勿問，下吏議帖堅妻與圓泰罪，既而以遠蠻俱釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered that Zongshou not be prosecuted, had officials discuss the crimes of Tie Jian's wife and Yuantai, and afterward, because they were distant barbarians, released them both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told officials to leave Zongshou alone and to determine the guilt of Tie Jian's widow and Yuantai, but in the end released them both as people from distant border regions.

sentences.zh: 久之，復有人告茂匿龍州未死，前宗壽所言皆妄。

translations.literal: After some time, someone again reported that Mao was hiding in Longzhou and had not died, and that everything Zongshou had said earlier was false.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, fresh reports arrived that Chang Mao was still alive in Longzhou and that Zongshou's earlier account had been entirely false.

sentences.zh: 遂詔右軍都督府榜諭宗壽及龍州官民，言：「昔鄭國公常茂有罪，上以開平王之功，不忍遽置於法，安置龍州。

translations.literal: The throne then ordered the Right Military Commission to post a proclamation to Zongshou and the officials and people of Longzhou, saying: "Formerly Duke of Zheng Guo Chang Mao was guilty, but the emperor, because of the merit of the Prince of Kaiping, could not bear to punish him at once and settled him at Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then had the Right Military Commission issue a proclamation to Zongshou and the officials and people of Longzhou, saying: "Formerly Chang Mao, Duke of Zheng, had committed crimes, but the emperor, honoring the Prince of Kaiping's service, would not punish him immediately and instead settled him at Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 土官趙帖堅故，其妻與茂結為婚姻，誘合諸蠻，肆為不道。

translations.literal: When the native official Zhao Tie Jian died, his wife formed a marriage alliance with Mao, incited the various barbarians, and wantonly did what was not right.
translations.idiomatic: After the native official Zhao Tie Jian died, his widow allied herself with Chang Mao by marriage, stirred up the border peoples, and committed one outrage after another.

sentences.zh: 帖堅侄宗壽襲職，與黃氏互相告訐，言茂已死。

translations.literal: Tie Jian's nephew Zongshou succeeded to office and, with Lady Huang, mutually accused each other, saying Mao was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Jian's nephew Zongshou inherited the post and exchanged accusations with Lady Huang, each claiming that Chang Mao was dead.

sentences.zh: 上以功臣子，猶加憐憫，釋二人告訐罪。

translations.literal: Because he was the son of a meritorious minister, the emperor still showed pity and released the two from the crime of mutual accusation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, still mindful that Chang Mao was a meritorious minister's son, showed mercy and released both accusers from punishment.

sentences.zh: 今有人言茂實未死，宗壽等知狀。

translations.literal: Now someone says Mao in fact has not died and that Zongshou and the others knew the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Now reports say Chang Mao is in fact still alive and that Zongshou and his party knew it all along.

sentences.zh: 已遣散騎舍人諭宗壽捕茂，延玩使者久不復命，其意莫測。

translations.literal: An attendant in regular cavalry has already been sent to instruct Zongshou to capture Mao, but he has kept the envoy waiting and long failed to reply; his intentions cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant of the Regular Cavalry has already been sent to order Zongshou to capture Chang Mao, yet he has kept the envoy waiting and for a long time sent no answer. His intentions are impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 特命榜諭爾宗壽等知之，如茂果存，則送至京師以贖罪，如茂果死，宗壽亦宜親率大小頭目至京，具陳其由。」

translations.literal: You, Zongshou and the others, are specially commanded to know this by proclamation: if Mao is indeed alive, send him to the capital to redeem your guilt; if Mao is indeed dead, Zongshou should also personally lead the great and small headmen to the capital and fully explain what happened."
translations.idiomatic: This proclamation is addressed especially to Zongshou and his party: if Chang Mao is still alive, send him to the capital to atone for your guilt; if he is truly dead, Zongshou must come in person with all the headmen, great and small, and explain the whole affair at court."

sentences.zh: 廣西布政司言宗壽屢詔赴京，拒命不出，又言南丹、奉議等蠻梗化。

translations.literal: The Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission reported that Zongshou, though repeatedly summoned to the capital by edict, refused the order and would not come out, and also said that the barbarians of Nandan, Fengyi, and other places were resisting civilization.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi administration reported that Zongshou had repeatedly defied imperial summons to the capital and also that the peoples of Nandan, Fengyi, and other districts were refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝復命致仕兵部尚書唐鐸往諭宗壽，訖不從命。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the retired Minister of War Tang Duo to go and instruct Zongshou, but in the end he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent the retired Minister of War Tang Duo to reason with Zongshou, but he still refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 詔發湖廣、江西所屬衛所馬步官軍六萬余，各賫三月糧，期以秋初俱赴廣西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered more than sixty thousand cavalry and infantry from the guard units subordinate to Huguang and Jiangxi, each carrying three months' grain, to assemble in Guangxi at the beginning of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized more than sixty thousand cavalry and infantry from the guard units of Huguang and Jiangxi, each man carrying three months' rations, to gather in Guangxi at the start of autumn.

sentences.zh: 命都督楊文佩征南將軍印，為總兵官，都指揮韓觀為左將軍，都督僉事宋晟為右將軍，劉真為參將，率京衛馬步軍三萬人至廣西，會討龍州及奉議、南丹、向武等州叛蠻。

translations.literal: It appointed Yang Wen bearer of the seal of General Who Pacifies the South as supreme commander, Han Guan as Left General, Song Sheng as Right General, and Liu Zhen as staff colonel, and ordered them to lead thirty thousand cavalry and infantry from the capital guards to Guangxi to join in suppressing the rebellious barbarians of Longzhou and of Fengyi, Nandan, Xiangwu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wen was given the seal of General Who Pacifies the South as supreme commander, with Han Guan as Left General, Song Sheng as Right General, and Liu Zhen as staff colonel. They were to lead thirty thousand capital guards to Guangxi and join the campaign against the rebel peoples of Longzhou, Fengyi, Nandan, Xiangwu, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 師行，帝撰文遣使祭嶽鎮海瀆，復遣禮部尚書任亨泰、監察御史嚴震直使安南，諭以討龍州趙宗壽之故，令陳日焜慎守邊境，毋助逆，勿納叛。

translations.literal: When the army set out, the emperor composed a text and sent envoys to offer sacrifice to the mountains and to the great rivers and seas, and again sent Minister of Rites Ren Hengtai and Censor Yan Zhenzhi as envoys to Annam to explain the reason for punishing Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, instructing Chen Rikun to guard the border carefully, not aid rebels, and not harbor fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: As the army marched, the emperor composed a ritual text and sent envoys to sacrifice to the sacred mountains and to the great rivers and seas. He also sent Minister of Rites Ren Hengtai and Censor Yan Zhenzhi to Annam to explain the campaign against Zhao Zongshou of Longzhou, warning Chen Rikun to hold the frontier strictly, give no aid to rebels, and shelter no fugitives.

sentences.zh: 遣人諭文調南寧衛兵千人，江陰侯吳高領之，柳州衛兵千人，安陸侯吳傑領之，皆令其建功自贖。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent ordering Wen to detach one thousand troops from Nanning Guard, to be led by Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao, and one thousand from Liuzhou Guard, to be led by Marquis of Anlu Wu Jie, all with orders to win merit and redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wen was also ordered to detach one thousand men from Nanning Guard under Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao, and one thousand from Liuzhou Guard under Marquis of Anlu Wu Jie, each charged to earn redemption through service.

sentences.zh: 又詔文等，如兵至龍州，宗壽親來見，具陳茂已死之由，則宥其罪。

translations.literal: An edict also told Wen and the others that if, when the army reached Longzhou, Zongshou came in person to see them and fully explained the reason Mao was dead, his guilt would be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further instructed Wen and his officers that if Zongshou came in person when the army reached Longzhou and gave a full account of Chang Mao's death, he would be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 若詐遣人來，則進兵討之。

translations.literal: If he deceitfully sent others in his place, then they were to advance the army and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: If he tried to deceive them by sending someone else, they were to press the attack and punish him.

sentences.zh: 既，鐸還京，言宗壽伏罪來朝，乞罷兵勿征。

translations.literal: Afterward Tang Duo returned to the capital and reported that Zongshou had confessed guilt and come to court, begging that the army be withdrawn and the campaign halted.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Duo then returned to the capital and reported that Zongshou had submitted, confessed guilt at court, and begged that the troops be stood down.

sentences.zh: 詔文移兵於奉議，仍命鐸至軍參軍事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wen to shift the army to Fengyi and again appointed Tang Duo to join the army and take part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict redirected Wen's army to Fengyi and again sent Tang Duo to the front to advise on the campaign.

sentences.zh: 宗壽偕耆民農裏等六十九人來朝謝罪，貢方物。

translations.literal: Zongshou came to court with sixty-nine elders including Nong Li to beg forgiveness and present tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshou then came to court with sixty-nine elders, including Nong Li, to beg forgiveness and present local tribute.

sentences.zh: 宗壽死，子景升襲。

translations.literal: When Zongshou died, his son Jingsheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongshou's death, his son Jingsheng inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 景升死，無嗣，以叔仁政襲。

translations.literal: When Jingsheng died without an heir, his uncle Renzheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsheng died without an heir, his uncle Renzheng took over.

sentences.zh: 仁政再傳為趙源，源死無子。

translations.literal: Renzheng passed the office down for two generations to Zhao Yuan; when Yuan died he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed through Renzheng for two generations to Zhao Yuan, who died without a son.

sentences.zh: 思恩土官岑浚率兵攻田州回，劫龍州，奪其印，納故知府源妻岑氏。

translations.literal: Cen Jun, native official of Sinan, led troops to attack Tianzhou, turned back, raided Longzhou, seized its seal, and took in Yuan's widow, Lady Cen.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Jun, the native official of Sinan, marched on Tianzhou, then swung back to raid Longzhou, seized its seal, and took Yuan's widow, Lady Cen, for himself.

sentences.zh: 詔下鎮巡官剿賊，而議立為源後者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered frontier pacification officials to suppress the bandits and also to consider who should be established as Yuan's successor.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered frontier officials to suppress the raiders and also to decide who should succeed Yuan.

sentences.zh: 以源庶兄浦有二子，相居長當立。

translations.literal: Because Yuan's elder half-brother Pu had two sons and the elder, Xiang, ought by seniority to succeed,
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's elder half-brother Pu had two sons, and the elder, Xiang, was the rightful heir by seniority.

sentences.zh: 相弟楷不能無望，則謀於岑氏，以仆韋隊子璋詭雲遺腹。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Kai could not be without ambition, so he plotted with Lady Cen and had the servant Wei Zhang's son Zhang falsely claimed as a posthumous son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother Kai, unwilling to accept this, conspired with Lady Cen and put forward the servant Wei Zhang's son Zhang as a supposed posthumous heir.

sentences.zh: 岑氏恃兄子猛方兵雄，楷遂奏言，璋實源子，當立，為相所篡。

translations.literal: Lady Cen relied on her brother's son Meng, whose forces were then strong; Kai then memorialized that Zhang was in fact Yuan's son and ought to succeed, and that Xiang had usurped the line.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cen leaned on her brother's son Meng, whose military power was then at its height. Kai memorialized that Zhang was Yuan's true son and rightful heir, and that Xiang had seized the succession by force.

sentences.zh: 事下督府勘，未決。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the supreme command for investigation, but no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the supreme command for investigation, but no ruling was reached.

sentences.zh: 璋賂鎮守太監傅倫舍人，詭稱有詔，檄猛調二萬兵，納璋入龍州。

translations.literal: Zhang bribed the resident grand eunuch Fu Lun's attendant and falsely claimed there was an edict, dispatching Meng to bring twenty thousand troops and install Zhang in Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang bribed an attendant of the resident grand eunuch Fu Lun and forged an edict calling up twenty thousand of Meng's troops to install him in Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 左江大震，相挈印奔況村。

translations.literal: The Left River region was greatly shaken, and Xiang fled with the seal to Kuang Village.
translations.idiomatic: The Left River region was thrown into uproar, and Xiang fled with the seal to Kuang Village.

sentences.zh: 都御史楊旦討璋，猛殺之，相乃歸。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Yang Dan moved against Zhang; Meng killed him, and Xiang then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Yang Dan marched against Zhang, but Meng killed him. Only then did Xiang return.

sentences.zh: 相二子，長遂，次寶。

translations.literal: Xiang had two sons: the elder Changsui and the younger Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had two sons: the elder Changsui and the younger Bao.

sentences.zh: 相枝拇，寶亦枝拇，相絕愛之，曰：「肖我當立。

translations.literal: Xiang had an extra thumb, and Bao also had an extra thumb. Xiang doted on him exceedingly and said: "He resembles me and ought to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had an extra thumb, and Bao did too. Xiang adored the boy and declared, "He is my very image and ought to inherit the post.

sentences.zh: 」猛乃以寶去，髡為奴。

translations.literal: " Meng then took Bao away and tonsured him as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng then carried Bao off and had him tonsured and kept as a slave.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，相死，州人立遂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, when Xiang died, the people of the prefecture installed Changsui.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1, after Xiang died, the people of Longzhou installed Changsui as ruler.

sentences.zh: 楷弒之，州人立其族弟暖。

translations.literal: Kai murdered him, and the people of the prefecture installed his clansman Nuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai assassinated him, and the people then installed his clansman Nuan.

sentences.zh: 時王守仁提督兩廣，幕客岑伯高用事，楷賂伯高，言暖非趙氏裔，當立者楷也。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shouren was grand coordinator of the two Guangs, and his staff member Cen Bogao held power. Kai bribed Bogao, saying Nuan was not of Zhao descent and that Kai himself ought to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren was then grand coordinator of the two Guangs, and his aide Cen Bogao held real sway. Kai bribed Bogao, claiming Nuan was no true Zhao and that he himself was the rightful heir.

sentences.zh: 遣上思州知州黃熊兆核之。

translations.literal: He sent the prefect of Shangsi Prefecture Huang Xiong Zhao to verify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Bogao sent Huang Xiong Zhao, prefect of Shangsi, to investigate.

sentences.zh: 熊兆黨伯高，言楷當立，以州印畀楷。

translations.literal: Huang Xiong Zhao sided with Bogao, said Kai ought to succeed, and handed over the prefectural seal to Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xiong Zhao sided with Bogao, ruled that Kai should succeed, and gave him the prefectural seal.

sentences.zh: 楷遂殺暖，龍州大亂。

translations.literal: Kai then killed Nuan, and Longzhou fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then murdered Nuan, and Longzhou descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 州目黃安等潛往田州購寶。

translations.literal: The prefectural officer Huang An and others secretly went to Tianzhou to purchase Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural officer Huang An and others secretly went to Tianzhou to buy Bao back.

sentences.zh: 寶時為奴楊布家十三年矣，安等行百金購得之。

translations.literal: Bao had by then been a slave in Yang Bu's household for thirteen years; An and the others paid one hundred taels of gold and obtained him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Bao had spent thirteen years as a slave in Yang Bu's household. Huang An and his party paid one hundred taels of gold and bought him out.

sentences.zh: 言之督府，都御史林富謂楷勢已張，毋持之急，乃令楷攝職，俟寶長讓之。

translations.literal: They reported the matter to the supreme command. Censor-in-chief Lin Fu said Kai's power was already strong and that he should not be pressed too hard; he therefore had Kai act in office temporarily, to yield the post when Bao came of age.
translations.idiomatic: They appealed to the supreme command. Censor-in-chief Lin Fu judged that Kai's power was already too great to confront directly, so he let Kai hold office temporarily on the understanding that he would yield to Bao when the boy came of age.

sentences.zh: 楷復，時時謀殺寶。

translations.literal: When Kai returned, he again and again plotted to kill Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Once back in power, Kai repeatedly plotted to kill Bao.

sentences.zh: 富諭楷，令以印還寶，寶謝以五千金，益以腴田三十一村。

translations.literal: Lin Fu instructed Kai to return the seal to Bao; Bao thanked him with five thousand taels of gold and added thirty-one rich villages.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fu ordered Kai to return the seal to Bao. Bao rewarded him with five thousand taels of gold and thirty-one fertile villages besides.

sentences.zh: 楷計寶弱易與，不如邀厚利而徐圖之，遂聽命。

translations.literal: Kai calculated that Bao was weak and easy to deal with and that it would be better to accept rich profit and scheme more slowly, so he obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Kai reckoned Bao weak and tractable, decided that large immediate gains were worth more than haste, and agreed.

sentences.zh: 楷復求韋璋之子應育之，令往來寶所。

translations.literal: Kai again asked for Wei Zhang's son Ying to be raised by him and sent to come and go at Bao's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Kai also asked to raise Wei Zhang's son Ying and sent him to move freely in and out of Bao's household.

sentences.zh: 寶妻黃氏，思明府土官黃朝女也，貳於寶而與應通。

translations.literal: Bao's wife Lady Huang was the daughter of Huang Chao, native official of Siming Prefecture. She was disloyal to Bao and had relations with Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's wife, Lady Huang, was the daughter of Huang Chao, native official of Siming Prefecture. She betrayed Bao and took Ying as her lover.

sentences.zh: 應乃厚結州目，又數遣人與向武州締好，乞兵為衛。

translations.literal: Ying then cultivated close ties with the prefectural officers and repeatedly sent men to Xiangwu Prefecture to establish friendship and beg troops for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Ying then won over the prefectural officers and repeatedly sent men to Xiangwu Prefecture to court alliance and ask for armed support.

sentences.zh: 寶日荒悍，刑狡男子王良為閽。

translations.literal: Day by day Bao grew wild and fierce; he punished a cunning man, Wang Liang, by making him gatekeeper.
translations.idiomatic: Bao grew daily more brutal and overbearing. He punished a shrewd man named Wang Liang by appointing him gatekeeper.

sentences.zh: 楷知良恨寶，激使內應，良許之。

translations.literal: When Kai learned that Liang resented Bao, he incited him to act as an inside agent, and Liang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liang hated Bao, Kai goaded him into serving as an inside agent, and Liang agreed.

sentences.zh: 楷以千人夜至寶寢門呼良，良開門納楷兵，執寶寢所，斬之，以他盜聞。

translations.literal: Kai came at night with one thousand men to the gate of Bao's sleeping quarters and called to Liang; Liang opened the gate and admitted Kai's troops, seized Bao in his bedchamber, beheaded him, and spread word that other bandits had done it.
translations.idiomatic: Kai came by night with a thousand men to the gate of Bao's quarters and called to Liang. Liang opened the gate, let the troops in, seized Bao in his bedchamber, and cut off his head, then spread word that ordinary bandits were to blame.

sentences.zh: 應以兵千人據州，並結朝自援。

translations.literal: Ying then occupied the prefecture with one thousand troops and also joined with Huang Chao to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ying then seized the prefecture with a thousand troops and enlisted Huang Chao's support.

sentences.zh: 都御史蔡經屬副使翁萬達謀之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Cai Jing entrusted Vice Commissioner Weng Wanda with planning the response.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Cai Jing put Vice Commissioner Weng Wanda in charge of the response.

sentences.zh: 萬達謂楷狙詐，未可速圖。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda said Kai was crafty and could not quickly be dealt with.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda judged Kai too cunning to be taken down quickly.

sentences.zh: 韋應巽懦寡慮，可旦夕擒，斷其中堅，然後可次第獲，督撫善之。

translations.literal: Wei Ying Sun was cowardly and lacked foresight; he could be captured in a day or two. Cut out the core and then the rest could be taken in order; the governor-general and grand coordinator approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ying Sun, he argued, was timid and shortsighted and could be seized within days. Remove the hard core first, and the rest would fall in sequence. The governor-general and grand coordinator agreed.

sentences.zh: 萬達行部至太平，使人以他事召朝，諭之計，論應當死，言楷才勇，正須藉為龍州當一面耳。

translations.literal: When Weng Wanda went on circuit to Taiping, he sent men to summon Huang Chao on another pretext, explained the plan to him, said Ying deserved death, and declared that Kai's talent and courage were just what Longzhou needed on its frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On circuit in Taiping, Weng Wanda summoned Huang Chao on a pretext, laid out the plan, told him Ying deserved death, and said Kai's talent and fighting spirit were exactly what Longzhou needed on its frontier.

sentences.zh: 時諸言楷事者，故不為理，州人大嘩。

translations.literal: At the time all who spoke of Kai's affair were deliberately ignored, and the people of the prefecture raised a great outcry.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile every petition about Kai's crimes was deliberately ignored, and the people of Longzhou erupted in protest.

sentences.zh: 萬達愈厚楷，楷信之，遂統精兵千人詣萬達言狀，並以三十一村地獻。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda treated Kai all the more generously; Kai trusted him and then led one thousand picked troops to Weng Wanda to explain the affair and also offered thirty-one villages of land.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda treated Kai with even greater favor. Trusting him, Kai led a thousand picked troops to report in person and offered up thirty-one villages.

sentences.zh: 萬達召楷及州目鄧瑀等入見，伏壯士劫之，曰：「汝罪大，宜自為計。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda summoned Kai and the prefectural officer Deng Yu and others to an audience, and hidden braves seized them by force, saying: "Your crime is grave; you should think for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Weng Wanda summoned Kai and prefectural officer Deng Yu and the others to an audience, where hidden strongmen seized them and said, "Your crimes are grave. You had better decide your own fate.

sentences.zh: 誠死，尚可為爾子留一官。

translations.literal: If you die willingly, your son may still be left an office.
translations.idiomatic: If you accept death, your son may still be left with an official post.

sentences.zh: 」楷自分無生理，乃手書諭其黨曰：「業已如此，亂無益也，可善輔我子以存趙。

translations.literal: " Kai judged that he had no way to live, and with his own hand wrote instructions to his faction: "Matters have already come to this; disorder will do no good. You should well support my son to preserve the Zhao line.
translations.idiomatic: " Kai saw no way to survive and wrote in his own hand to his followers: "Things have come to this pass; further rebellion will do no good. Support my son faithfully and preserve the Zhao line.

sentences.zh: 」萬達即杖楷，斃之，以楷書諭其州人。

translations.literal: " Weng Wanda immediately had Kai beaten with rods until he died, and used Kai's letter to instruct the people of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Weng Wanda then had Kai beaten to death with rods and circulated Kai's letter among the people of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 時楷子匡時，生四年矣，立之，一州悉定。

translations.literal: At the time Kai's son Kuangshi was four years old; he was installed, and the whole prefecture was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Kuangshi was then only four years old. Once he was installed, the whole prefecture quieted.

sentences.zh: 乃以十三村還龍州，十八村隸崇善縣，於是龍州趙氏仍得襲。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirteen villages were returned to Longzhou and eighteen villages were assigned to Chongshan County, and thus the Zhao line of Longzhou was again able to succeed hereditarily.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen villages were returned to Longzhou and eighteen were annexed to Chongshan County, and the Zhao line of Longzhou was once again established in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 歸順州，舊為峒，隸鎮安府。

translations.literal: Guishun Prefecture was formerly a dong and was subordinate to Zhen'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guishun Prefecture had originally been a dong subordinate to Zhen'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，鎮安知府岑誌綱分其第二子岑永綱領峒事，傳子瑛，屢率兵報效。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era, Zhen'an Prefect Cen Zhigang assigned his second son Cen Yonggang to administer the dong. It passed to his son Ying, who repeatedly led troops in service to the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Zhen'an Prefect Cen Zhigang put his second son Cen Yonggang in charge of the dong. The line passed to Yonggang's son Ying, who repeatedly led troops in the dynasty's service.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年，總督鄧廷瓚言：「鎮安府之歸順峒，舊為州治，洪武初裁革。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi, Governor-General Deng Tingzan said: "The Guishun dong of Zhen'an Prefecture was formerly a prefectural seat and was abolished at the beginning of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 9, Governor-General Deng Tingzan memorialized: "The Guishun dong of Zhen'an Prefecture was once a prefectural seat, abolished at the start of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 今其峒主岑瑛每效勞於官，乞設州治，授以土官知州。

translations.literal: Now its dong chief Cen Ying repeatedly renders service to the government. I beg that a prefectural seat be established and that he be appointed native prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief, Cen Ying, has repeatedly served the court well. I ask that the prefecture be restored and that he be appointed native prefect.

sentences.zh: 凡出兵令備土兵五千，仍歲領土兵二千赴梧州聽調。

translations.literal: Whenever troops are dispatched he should maintain five thousand native soldiers in readiness, and each year two thousand native soldiers should proceed to Wuzhou to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever troops are called out, he should keep five thousand native soldiers ready for duty, and each year send two thousand native soldiers to Wuzhou to await orders.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，增設流官吏目一員。

translations.literal: " The edict granted this and added one regular official assistant.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved and added one regular official assistant to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑛死，子璋襲。

translations.literal: When Ying died, his son Zhang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying's death, his son Zhang inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 復從璋奏，以本州改隸布政司。

translations.literal: Again following Zhang's memorial, the prefecture was reassigned to the Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang's further petition, the prefecture was placed directly under the Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 璋多智略。

translations.literal: Zhang was greatly skilled in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was a man of considerable strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 田州岑猛以不法獲譴，都御史姚鏌將舉兵討之。

translations.literal: Cen Meng of Tianzhou, for unlawful conduct, received reproof, and Censor-in-chief Yao Mo was about to raise troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Meng of Tianzhou had been censured for misconduct, and Censor-in-chief Yao Mo was preparing to march against him.

sentences.zh: 璋，猛婦翁也。

translations.literal: Zhang was Meng's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was Meng's father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 鏌慮璋黨猛，召都指揮沈希儀謀。

translations.literal: Yao Mo feared Zhang would side with Meng and summoned Commander Shen Xiyi to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Mo feared Zhang would take Meng's side and summoned Commander Shen Xiyi to consult.

sentences.zh: 希儀雅知璋女失寵，恨猛，又知部下千戶趙臣雅善璋。

translations.literal: Shen Xiyi already knew well that Zhang's daughter had lost favor and hated Meng, and also knew that his subordinate chiliarch Zhao Chen was on excellent terms with Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xiyi knew that Zhang's daughter had fallen out of favor and resented Meng, and that his chiliarch Zhao Chen was on close terms with Zhang.

sentences.zh: 希儀因使趙臣語璋圖猛，璋受命。

translations.literal: Shen Xiyi therefore had Zhao Chen speak with Zhang about plotting against Meng, and Zhang accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xiyi therefore sent Zhao Chen to propose a plot against Meng, and Zhang agreed.

sentences.zh: 時猛子邦彥守工堯隘，璋詐遣兵千人助邦彥，言：「天兵至，以姻黨故，且與爾同禍。

translations.literal: At the time Meng's son Bangyan guarded Gongyao Pass. Zhang falsely sent one thousand troops to aid Bangyan, saying: "The imperial army is coming. Because of our marriage tie we shall share the same disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's son Bangyan was then holding Gongyao Pass. Zhang sent a thousand men under false pretenses to reinforce him, saying, "The imperial army is coming. Because of our kinship by marriage, we shall share the same fate.

sentences.zh: 今發精兵來，幸努力堅守。

translations.literal: I have now sent picked troops; strive hard to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: I have sent elite troops to you now. Hold the pass with all your strength.

sentences.zh: 」邦彥欣納之。

translations.literal: " Bangyan gladly accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: " Bangyan accepted them gladly.

sentences.zh: 璋遣人報希儀曰：「謹以千人內應矣。

translations.literal: Zhang sent men to report to Shen Xiyi: "I have carefully placed one thousand men inside as collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang then sent word to Shen Xiyi: "As arranged, one thousand men are now inside as collaborators.

sentences.zh: 」時田州兵殊死拒戰，諸將莫利當隘者，希儀獨引兵當之。

translations.literal: " At that time the Tianzhou troops fought to the death in resistance. None of the generals wished to hold the pass, but Xi Yi alone led troops to block it.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Tianzhou soldiers were fighting with desperate fury. No other general would take the narrow pass, but Xi Yi marched forward alone to meet them.

sentences.zh: 約戰三合，歸順兵大呼曰：「敗矣！

translations.literal: After roughly three rounds of combat, the Guishun troops shouted loudly: "We are defeated!
translations.idiomatic: After about three clashes, the Guishun soldiers suddenly roared, "We're beaten!

sentences.zh: 」田州兵驚潰，希儀麾兵乘之，斬首數千級，邦彥死焉。

translations.literal: " The Tianzhou troops panicked and fled in rout. Xi Yi waved his troops forward in pursuit, beheading several thousand; Bangyan died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianzhou ranks broke in panic. Xi Yi drove his men in pursuit, taking several thousand heads; Bangyan fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 猛聞敗，欲自經。

translations.literal: When Meng heard of the defeat, he wished to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng learned of the rout, he tried to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 而璋先已築別館，使人請猛。

translations.literal: But Zhang had already built a separate lodge and sent someone to summon Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, however, had already prepared a separate residence and sent men to fetch Meng.

sentences.zh: 時猛倉皇不知所出，遂挈印從璋，使走歸順。

translations.literal: At that time Meng, in frantic haste and not knowing what course to take, took his seal and followed Zhang, who had him flee to Guishun.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, bewildered and with nowhere to turn, clutched his seal and went with Zhang, who hurried him off to Guishun.

sentences.zh: 璋詭為猛草奏，促猛出印實封之。

translations.literal: Zhang forged a memorial on Meng's behalf and pressed Meng to produce his seal and seal it in an official envelope for dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang secretly drafted a memorial in Meng's name and pressed him to bring out his seal and have it affixed and sealed for sending.

sentences.zh: 璋既知猛印所在，乃鴆殺猛，斬其首，並府印函之，間道馳軍門。

translations.literal: Once Zhang knew where Meng's seal was, he poisoned Meng, cut off his head, placed it together with the prefectural seal in a case, and raced by a secret route to the army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang had learned where the seal was kept, he poisoned Meng, severed his head, packed it with the prefectural seal, and galloped by a hidden route to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 為讒言所阻，竟不論功。

translations.literal: Obstructed by slander, he was never rewarded for his service in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Slander blocked his reward, and in the end his deeds went unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 璋死，次子瓛襲。

translations.literal: When Zhang died, his second son Huan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang's death, his second son Huan inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，提督盛應期以瓛先助猛逆攻泗城，許自新，出兵討賊自贖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi, because Huan had earlier assisted the rebel Meng in attacking Sicheng, granted him opportunity to reform and ordered him to dispatch troops to suppress bandits and redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 4, Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi noted that Huan had once aided the rebel Meng against Sicheng. He allowed him to make amends and sent him out to fight bandits in expiation.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十四年，四州盧蘇叛，糾瓛攻鎮安府。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Lu Su of the Four Prefectures rebelled and incited Huan to attack Zhen'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Lu Su of the Four Prefectures rose in revolt and drew Huan into an assault on Zhen'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瓛破鎮安，並發岑真寶父母墳墓。

translations.literal: Huan captured Zhen'an and also dug up the graves of Cen Zhenbao's parents.
translations.idiomatic: Huan overran Zhen'an and even opened the tombs of Cen Zhenbao's parents.

sentences.zh: 事聞，革冠帶，許立功贖。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, his official cap and belt were revoked, but he was permitted to redeem himself through meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Once word reached the court, his cap and belt were stripped, though he was told he might win them back by distinguished service.

sentences.zh: 瓛後從征交阯，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Huan later joined the campaign against Jiaozhi and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Huan later marched on the Jiaozhi campaign and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 子代襲，萬歷間以貢馬違限，給半賞。

translations.literal: His son Dai succeeded him. During the Wanli reign, for delivering tribute horses past the deadline, he was granted only half the usual reward.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dai succeeded him. In the Wanli era he brought tribute horses late and received only half the customary reward.

sentences.zh: 向武州，宋置，隸橫山寨。

translations.literal: Xiangwu Prefecture was established in the Song and was subordinate to Hengshan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwu Prefecture was founded in Song times and answered to Hengshan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 元隸田州路。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it was subordinate to Tianzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it fell under Tianzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其界東北抵田州，西抵鎮安，南抵鎮遠。

translations.literal: Its borders: to the northeast it adjoined Tianzhou, to the west Zhen'an, and to the south Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Its frontiers met Tianzhou to the northeast, Zhen'an to the west, and Zhenyuan to the south.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年七月，土官黃世鐵遣使貢馬及方物。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Hongwu, the native official Huang Shitie sent envoys to present horses and local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Hongwu 2, the native official Huang Shitie sent tribute horses and regional goods.

sentences.zh: 詔以世鐵為向武州知州，許世襲。

translations.literal: An imperial decree appointed Shitie magistrate of Xiangwu Prefecture, with permission for hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Shitie magistrate of Xiangwu Prefecture and allowed the office to pass in his line.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廣西布政司言向武州叛蠻梗化。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the Guangxi Provincial Administration Commission reported that rebellious barbarians in Xiangwu Prefecture were obstructing assimilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Guangxi administration reported that rebel tribes in Xiangwu were resisting civilization.

sentences.zh: 時都督楊文佩征南將軍印，討龍州、奉議等處，復奉命移師向武。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Commander Yang Wen, bearing the seal of General Who Pacifies the South, was suppressing Longzhou, Fengyi, and other places, and was again ordered to shift his army to Xiangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Yang Wen, who held the seal of the Pacifying-South General, was then campaigning in Longzhou, Fengyi, and elsewhere when he was ordered to turn his army toward Xiangwu.

sentences.zh: 文調右副將軍韓觀分兵進討都康、向武、富勞諸州縣，斬世鐵。

translations.literal: Yang Wen dispatched Right Vice General Han Guan to lead troops separately against Dukang, Xiangwu, Fulao, and other prefectures and counties, and Shitie was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wen sent Right Vice General Han Guan with divided forces against Dukang, Xiangwu, Fulao, and other districts; Shitie was executed.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書唐鐸言，置向武州守禦千戶所。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Minister of War Tang Duo, a Xiangwu Prefecture Guard and Defense Battalion of a thousand households was established.
